title: Stop a pane's systemd scope when the pane closes or is released
notes:
Part 3 of 4 (after part 1 merges): stop a pane's scope when the pane closes or is released.

pane.close and pane.release (src/main/actions/pane/) stop the pane's recorded scope with `systemctl --user stop <unit>` after the shell ends, so a dev server or watcher the agent detached goes too (today it outlives the pane). A scope that is already gone is fine. Through the pane actions only (actions-rule-1). A scope survives an app restart like the pane host's shells; pane.restore re-reads its unit name. No scope recorded (fallback, Windows, macOS): nothing to stop.
Tests: the decision (which unit to stop, when, none recorded) pure with tests; the systemctl call behind a port. Hand check: start `sleep 1000 &` disowned in an agent pane, release the pane, the sleep is gone. Docs: docs/processes, panes README, history.
Engineering bar: clean, testable, readable.
